meaning: A square pattern of tiny black and white boxes. Point your phone camera at it to open a web page, see a menu, or pay.
clues: You hold your phone up near it to use it.
It can carry a web address or other data for your phone to read.
You can see it: a square of small black and white boxes, printed or on a screen.
A company in Japan invented it. Car makers were early users.
It is a two-word name that starts with Q.
assumes: A grocery barcode is made of black stripes

decoys.meaning: The pattern of black stripes on a product that a store scanner reads to find the item and its price.
Hold your phone near a store's card reader to pay with a card saved on your phone.
A tiny chip in a small tag. Hold your phone very close, and it reads what's stored there, like a web link.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Try it: point your phone's camera at one on a menu or a sign. Read the web address that pops up before you tap it.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: The stripes on a grocery item were a code too. A scanner read them and the price showed up at the register. This square does that job and holds much more.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Skip ones that come in a text or email you didn't expect. And if one looks stuck on top of another, stop and ask someone.
